title: Customer Request Decision Fabric for Private Deployments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Customers requesting Private/VPC/on-prem deployments create high-touch triage work: network verification, airgap constraints, upgrade windows, and SLA expectations. Current intake is manual, inconsistent across regions, and causes long lead times and surprise blockers for Eng and Solutions teams.

Goal: Ship a decision fabric that automates initial triage, surfaces explainable priority scores, runs lightweight self-serve probes, and produces a recommended engagement lane (self-serve, concierge, blocked, fast-track) with prescriptive remediation steps. The fabric should reduce manual triage load by 60% and time-to-first-response by 50% for network-related requests.

Scope: Non-bug product requests relating to Private/VPC/on-prem deployments (networking, upgrades, air-gapped constraints, proxy/bridge patterns). Out of scope: full infra provisioning, implementation work owned by Dedicated/on-prem engineering teams, and legal/contract negotiations.

Deliverables:
- Intake form revision (probe-first questions + machine-readable signals)
- Probe-as-code library (SSH/tcp/http probes, proxy handshake, cert checks) that customers can run and upload results
- Scoring engine prototype with explainable weights and audit trail
- Operator UI: request summary + recommended lane + three suggested remediation steps + estimated lead time
- Runbook mapping from lane -> SLA/next steps -> escalation path

Approach:
1) Define minimal probe set and machine-readable fields (region, network egress, firewall rules, proxy type, upgrade window).
2) Build lightweight probe runner (containerized) customers can run; collect results (red/amber/green) and attach to ticket automatically.
3) Implement scoring rules: base score from business signals (annual spend, data sensitivity), network readiness score from probe results, upgrade risk from version matrix. Prefer deterministic, auditable rules rather than black-box ML in MVP.
4) Surface recommended lane in operator UI with reasons and suggested remediation tasks (e.g., open port 443 on gateway, provide NAT details, schedule 2-hour maintenance window).
5) Pilot with 3 enterprise customers and the Solutions onboarding team; iterate on thresholds and UI text.

Success metrics:
- 60% reduction in manual triage touchpoints for network-related requests
- Median time-to-first-response <= 24 hours for prioritized requests
- Operator acceptance: >= 80% of recommendations accepted or require minor edits
- Pilot feedback NPS >= +40 on intake experience

Stakeholders: PM (Aisha Patel), Solutions Eng (Maya Chen), Edge/Networking Eng (Ravi Singh), Security (Claire Huang), Console UX (Evelyn Park), Legal (as needed).
acceptance_criteria: Intake form updated and deployed to self-serve portal
Probe-as-code runner v0.1 published with docs and sample outputs
Scoring engine produces lane + explainability for 95% of incoming private deploy requests during pilot
Operator UI displays decision, three remediation actions, and an audit trail link
Pilot with 3 customers completed and results documented (lessons + thresholds)
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers unwilling/unable to run probes — Mitigation: provide concierge-run option and lightweight remote-probe alternative
Risk: False negatives from probes blocking eligible customers — Mitigation: manual override with documented justification and fast appeal path
Risk: Exposure of sensitive config in probe outputs — Mitigation: probe redacts PII and includes an opt-in encrypted upload path; Security sign-off required
Risk: Scoring perceived as opaque — Mitigation: every score is accompanied by a human-readable rationale and the individual signal contributions
